data.title: Propanc Biopharma Arranges $3 Million Convertible Note Financing for $2.1 Million
data.description:
Propanc Biopharma agreed to issue convertible notes with $3 million in aggregate principal and warrants for a total subscription amount of $2.1 million, including $2 million in cash from Eleven 11 Management and $100,000 in credits from Hexstone Capital. At the initial November 20 closing, the company issued notes totaling $2.22 million in principal and warrants for 1,268,573 shares; an additional $780,000 in subscriptions is planned for a second closing subject to conditions. The notes carry 14% annual interest, mature August 20, 2027, and have an initial conversion price of $1.75 per share. Hexstone also waived certain existing restrictions and consented to the transactions.

Agreement 1: Propanc Biopharma Secures $2 Million Cash Financing From Eleven 11

  • Agreement type: Securities purchase agreement for convertible notes and warrants
  • Counterparty: Eleven 11 Management
  • Signed / Effective: Nov 20 2026 / same
  • Duration / Termination: Notes mature Aug 20 2027; warrants expire four years after issuance
  • Reason: Raise financing through convertible notes and warrants

Agreement 2: Propanc Biopharma Arranges $100,000 Hexstone Subscription Through Credits

  • Agreement type: Securities purchase agreement for convertible notes and warrants
  • Counterparty: Hexstone Capital
  • Signed / Effective: Nov 20 2026 / same
  • Duration / Termination: Notes mature Aug 20 2027; warrants expire four years after issuance
  • Reason: Provide financing through credited subscription consideration

Agreement 3: Propanc Biopharma Obtains Hexstone Consent and Waiver for Financing

data.title: Treasury Yields Gain As U.S. Equities Rally — Market Talk
data.description: U.S. Treasury yields recover from their pre-Thanksgiving retreat and move higher as equities post Black Friday gains and the U.S. dollar strengthens. Data in the holiday-shortened week included an upward revision in U.S. 3Q GDP and a PCE inflation reading in line with estimates, which supported strong expectations the Fed will raise interest rates on Dec. 9. "The Fed still has a long way to go to get inflation back to its 2% target," Brown Brothers Harriman says in a note. An equity correction alone is unlikely to stop the Fed from tightening, the firm says. "The Fed's hawkish policy stance is intact and supportive of USD." The 10-year Treasury yield rises 8.7 basis points to 4.933%, up 2.4 basis points on the week. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

data.title: Quantum Space to Hold Financial Update Call
data.description:

data.title: Canadian Securities Exchange Welcomes Listing of Quantum Vault Holding Corp.
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - The Canadian Securities Exchange ("CSE" or "the Exchange") today welcomed the listing of Quantum Vault Holding Corp. ("Quantum" or the "Company"), following the Toronto-based Company's recent completion of a reverse takeover of Rigel Technologies Inc. Quantum's shares began trading on the CSE yesterday under the ticker symbol QVT, and today, the Quantum team opened the market: https://youtu.be/n4xNVLUpuRc.

Quantum is a technology company developing hardware and software security solutions intended to address cybersecurity challenges associated with future quantum computer development. The Company is focused on securing current infrastructure against advances in quantum computing by developing security features intended to follow recognized standards and address existing cybersecurity threats that may evolve over time, while building a foundation for long-term quantum resilience.

"AI, quantum computing and hyperconnectivity are driving business productivity, but also exposing critical infrastructure to unforeseen risks that require innovative solutions," said Stuart Schady, the CSE's Vice President, Business Development. "The CSE is an established exchange for emerging technology companies and Quantum joins a growing group of such companies. We welcome the Quantum team to the CSE."

"This is just the start for us," said David Posner, Chief Executive Officer of Quantum. "We're really excited to start trading on the CSE and show the market what we're all about."

"The more dependent we become on the internet, the more important it is to protect it," added Nauman Arshad, the Company's Chief Technology Officer. "At Quantum Vault, we've developed an innovative product designed for the emerging post-AI, post-quantum era. Our mandate is to build compact, rugged, embedded security modules that will help keep the internet safe and secure for many years to come."

The Canadian Securities Exchange is a rapidly growing exchange invested in working with entrepreneurs, innovators and disruptors to access public capital markets in Canada. The Exchange's efficient operating model, advanced technology and competitive fee structure help its listed issuers of all sectors and sizes minimize their cost of capital and enhance global liquidity.

data.title: CME cattle higher on strength from equity markets
data.description:
By Heather Schlitz

Chicago Mercantile Exchange live and feeder cattle futures turned higher on Friday amid a light trade and spillover strength from equity markets.

Cattle futures also benefited from a short-covering driven rebound after a slide in previous days.

Wall Street's main indexes ended higher on Friday and posted weekly gains as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday and flocked to hard-hit AI-linked shares. US stocks have swung sharply this week.

Traders continue to closely monitor consumer beef demand as the protein becomes pricier.

"We've seen light pushback from consumers the past two months but we haven't seen it collapse," said Rich Nelson, chief strategist at Allendale.

Restaurant traffic and retail purchases of beef can slow when consumers are worried about inflation and the broader economy.

CME February live cattle futures settled 1.15 cents higher at 228.125 cents per pound. CME January feeder cattle settled 3.675 cents higher at 331.20 cents per pound.

The choice boxed beef cutout rose 64 cents to $357.23 per hundredweight, and the select cutout rose $2.36 to $347.07 per cwt, according to the US Department of Agriculture on Friday afternoon.

The USDA said on Tuesday the US frozen beef supply on October 31 was up 5% from a month earlier and up 2% from a year ago, even as cattle marketing declined in the month. The data suggested beef demand has slowed, analysts said.

Trade volume has been relatively light between Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday and the weekend. Grain markets were closed for Thanksgiving and traded for an abbreviated session on Friday.

Most-active February hogs (LHG27) settled 0.575 cent higher at 56 cents per pound.

The pork carcass cutout value rose 92 cents to $67.90 per cwt, USDA data showed.

data.title: Natuzzi Ordinary and Extraordinary Shareholders’ Meeting
data.description:
Natuzzi S.p.A. (NYSE:NTZ) (“Natuzzi” or the “Company”), one of the most renowned brands in the production and distribution of design and luxury furniture, today announces that its ordinary and extraordinary shareholders’ meeting (the “Meeting”) was held on November 23, 2026, at the Company’s registered office in Santeramo in Colle (Bari), Italy, and approved all the items on the agenda, as described below.

Extraordinary Shareholders’ Meeting

Reserved Capital Increase. The Meeting approved a capital increase for consideration, in cash, on an indivisible basis, with the exclusion of pre-emptive rights pursuant to Article 2441, paragraph 5, of the Italian Civil Code, reserved for Invest 2003 S.r.l. (“INVEST”), for a total amount of EUR 17,499,998.73 (of which EUR 491,159.10 is allocated to share capital and EUR 17,008,839.63 to share premium) (the “Reserved Capital Increase”), through the issuance of 49,115,910 new ordinary shares at an issue price of EUR 0.3563 per share (approximately US$2.06 per American Depositary Share).

The new shares were paid up in full through the application of the equity reserve earmarked in favor of INVEST, resulting from the irrevocable reclassification of EUR 12.5 million and EUR 5 million of shareholder loans on March 31, 2026 and September 9, 2026, respectively, as capital contributions towards a future capital increase, without any further cash contribution. The new shares will have the same characteristics and dividend entitlement as the outstanding shares.

As previously disclosed, the Reserved Capital Increase forms part of the corporate steps being taken by the Company in connection with its request for review of the New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”) delisting determination filed on September 10, 2026.

The Reserved Capital Increase was subscribed for in full by INVEST on November 26, 2026 and is fully paid up as of the date hereof, with only the related filing formalities with the competent Companies Register remaining outstanding.

Delegated Rights Issues. The Meeting granted the Board of Directors authority, pursuant to Article 2443 of the Italian Civil Code, to increase the share capital for consideration, in cash, on a divisible basis, on one or more occasions, by June 30, 2027, through two separate rights issues to be offered on a pre-emptive basis to those entitled thereto:

(a) up to a maximum amount of EUR 15,000,000, including share premium, to be offered to all shareholders on a pre-emptive basis and structured to allow minority shareholders, upon full subscription, to restore their percentage shareholdings prior to the Reserved Capital Increase, subject to INVEST’s prior waiver of its pre-emptive rights, described below (the “Delegated Rights Issue for Minorities”); and

(b) up to a maximum amount of EUR 65,000,000, including share premium, through the issuance of up to 1,300,000,000 ordinary shares, to be offered to all shareholders on a pre-emptive basis, with the Board of Directors determining the issue price, terms and timing (the “Delegated Rights Issue”).

As previously disclosed, the Delegated Rights Issue, contemplated by the compliance plan accepted by the NYSE, as announced by the Company on May 22, 2026, is intended to (i) strengthen the Company’s capital structure and enable it to regain compliance, before July 6, 2027, with the US$50,000,000 average global market capitalization or stockholders’ equity standard set out in Section 802.01B of the NYSE Listed Company Manual; and (ii) raise funds to support the Company’s cash flow performance and the successful outcome of the composizione negoziata della crisi (CNC) proceedings, as part of the restructuring process.

The Delegated Rights Issue and the Delegated Rights Issue for Minorities both presuppose the successful completion of the Reserved Capital Increase and are independent and non-alternative: the Board of Directors may exercise either or both of the authorities, depending on the Company’s capital strengthening needs, market conditions and the progress of the restructuring process.

In connection with the Delegated Rights Issue for Minorities, INVEST delivered to the Company a conditional and limited waiver, dated November 4, 2026, of the pre-emptive rights to which it would be entitled in the Delegated Rights Issue for Minorities (the “Waiver”). The Waiver is limited to the number of ordinary shares necessary to enable shareholders other than INVEST, in the event of full subscription, to restore their respective percentage shareholdings held immediately prior to the Reserved Capital Increase.

The Waiver’s effectiveness is subject to the satisfaction of the conditions precedent specified therein, including completion of the Reserved Capital Increase and issuance of the corresponding ordinary shares to INVEST. The Waiver requires that the Delegated Rights Issue for Minorities be resolved upon by the Board of Directors, subscribed for and paid up by June 30, 2027, without any automatic or unilateral extension, and does not extend to shares issued in excess of the applicable rebalancing limit.

The Waiver does not extend to the Delegated Rights Issue or to any other capital increase, and INVEST retains its pre-emptive and other rights in respect of such transactions. The Waiver does not constitute a commitment by INVEST to (i) subscribe for any additional ordinary shares, (ii) provide further funding to the Company or (iii) subscribe for any unsubscribed shares.

Elimination of Nominal Value. The Meeting approved the elimination of the indication of the nominal value of the Company’s ordinary shares, previously EUR 1.00 each, which according to Italian law constituted a minimum issue price for new shares, thereby providing flexibility in setting the issue price both for the Reserved Capital Increase and for any subsequent rights issues.

The resolutions adopted at the extraordinary session of the Meeting and described above will take effect upon their registration with the competent Companies Register, which the Company expects to occur in the coming days.

Ordinary Shareholders’ Meeting

Appointment of a Statutory Auditor. The Meeting appointed Mr. Vito Plantone as a standing member of the Board of Statutory Auditors, following the resignation of Mr. Francesco Campobasso. Mr. Plantone will remain in office until the expiration of the term of the current Board of Statutory Auditors, which will occur upon approval of the Company’s financial statements for the year ending December 31, 2027.

data.title: Why Qualys stock is trading up today
data.description:
What happened?

Shares of cybersecurity cloud platform provider Qualys jumped 6.6% in the morning session after a rebound in technology stocks lifted major U.S. equity indexes during a holiday-shortened trading session.

CNBC reported that the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged higher by 1.18% to 50,774.94, the S&P 500 edged higher by 1.6% to 7,297.49 and the Nasdaq Composite climbed 2.31% to 24,129.50. According to the report, U.S. exchanges closed early following the Thanksgiving holiday, while the Dow and S&P 500 finished the week up more than 5% and the Nasdaq gained more than 6%.

Technology stocks led the advance, as Meta Platforms rose more than 3%, Amazon rose about 4%, Broadcom rose almost 4% and Anthropic soared nearly 11%, the report said. The rebound followed earlier market weakness tied to investor concerns over artificial intelligence debt financing, signs of moderation in capital expenditures and expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate increases, according to the report.

Broader rallies in technology stocks can lift investor sentiment toward software companies across the market. When buyers return to growth-oriented sectors after a pullback, share prices of individual technology businesses often move higher together.

After the initial pop, the shares cooled down and closed the day at $206.60, up 5.2% from the previous close.

What is the market telling us

Qualys’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 39 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 4 days ago when the stock gained 5.5% on the news that CrowdStrike announced a definitive all-stock transaction valued at approximately $43.9 billion to acquire Zscaler, uniting endpoint protection and zero-trust network security.

The mega-deal marks one of the largest consolidation moves in software history, directly influencing cybersecurity valuations across public markets. By integrating Zscaler into its Falcon platform, CrowdStrike aims to offer an all-in-one security architecture that protects both devices and cloud network traffic. Zero-trust security operates on the principle of never trusting and always verifying any user or device attempting to access private networks.

For investors, this massive transaction underscores escalating enterprise demand for comprehensive cybersecurity suites rather than fragmented point solutions, driving heightened interest and trading activity in both companies.

Qualys is up 68.1% since the beginning of the year, and at $220.23 per share, it is trading close to its 52-week high of $230.29 from October 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Qualys’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,639.

data.title: Robusta coffee heads away from 3-year low; raw sugar gains 10% weekly
data.description:
Robusta coffee futures on ICE headed further away from this week's 3-year lows on Friday amid lacklustre farmer selling in top grower Vietnam, while raw sugar posted a 10.2% price gain this week, recovering from a three-month low last week.

COFFEE

* Robusta coffee settled up $91, or 3.2%, at $2,923 a metric ton, after setting a 3-year low of $2,709 on Wednesday.

* "Farmers are increasingly reluctant to sell," said a dealer based in Vietnam.

* He explained that if prices don't recover, he expects farmers to sell at most 35% of their crop before the Tet holiday in February, as they are banking on this year's dry weather and next year's El Nino peak to tighten supplies.

* Arabica coffee rose 2.1% to $2.7555 per lb, after hitting a five-month low on Wednesday.

* Dealers noted a sharp recovery in the Brazilian currency following the appointment of a new finance minister. The real gained 9% this week.

* "A stronger real gives Brazilian producers fewer reais per dollar sold. That tends to slow farmer selling and support flat price," said Tomas Araujo, a broker with StoneX.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar (SBH7) settled up 0.43 cent, or 2.3%, at 18.77 cents per lb, having hit a fresh one-month high of 19.10 cents earlier. The market gained 10.2% this week.

* France's main sugar groups Tereos and Cristal Union have offered financial support to beet growers hit by drought and heatwaves, seeking to maintain plantings for the 2027 crop as Europe faces a sugar shortfall.

* The gains in the Brazilian currency also offered support to the sugar market, dealers said.

* The global sugar deficit in the 2026/27 season will be slightly larger than previously expected, with a weaker outlook for production in India, Green Pool forecast.

* Itau BBA has cut its forecast for sugarcane crushing in Brazil's key center-south region in 2026/27 to between 620 million and 640 million metric tons, down from 645 million tons.

* White sugar rose 0.6% to $525.40 a ton, having hit a fresh one-month high of $534.40 earlier.

COCOA

* London cocoa ​settled up £71, or 1.7%, to £4,291 per ton, having hit its highest since late October at £4,335.

* The supply outlook continues to worsen in top growers Ivory Coast, Ghana and Ecuador, though there is ample availability of cocoa for now from the bumper 2025/26 crop.

* New York cocoa rose 1.2% to $5,499 a ton.

data.title: Silver Price Analysis: XAG/USD Faces Deeper Losses as $40 Support Nears
data.description:
The week's fall in silver prices highlights the fragility of the market. This week's slide in silver prices is a sign of the market's fragility.

Silver’s Weekly Decline Exposes a Weakening Market

Silver has continued its downward trend, falling 15.37% over the past week to around $41.23 per ounce, as seen on the Trading Economics chart.

The Investing.com daily chart also shows silver lost 3.86% during the session, ending around $41.20 after the lowest price it hit during today's session was $40.77.

The higher-level chart pattern indicates a long-term return from the August highs around $70. Source: TradingEconomics

Since then, successive lower highs and lower lows have been observed, suggesting that sellers have been in control. The drop was picked up after the metal's recovery in November collapsed, taking the price back towards the $53 mark.

The price is in line with the overall decline of precious metals. The drop in gold and silver prices was blamed in a November 21 Wall Street Journal report on rising interest rates for U.S. government bonds and a stronger U.S. dollar and on additional rate increases by the Federal Reserve. Silver's industrial ties make it a weak performer when investors are nervous about economic growth, too.

Technical Outlook: $40 Becomes the Next Major Test

The daily chart shows a bearish pattern with the price of silver moving into the lower part of the range shown and near the bottom of the daily consolidation range. The first significant support reference is the latest session's low at $40.77. The next psychological level that traders should pay attention to is $40 below.

However, if silver continues to close below $40 every day, it could bring additional downside pressure to silver and further confirm the ongoing series of lower lows. But if there is a temporary drop below support with a fast bounce up, it might mean that the buyers are trying to cover the selling pressure.

According to the chart, the positive side is that 42.80–43.60 seems to be a point of initial resistance as per the opening and higher levels of the recent daily trading session. Source: investing.com

If the price can resume its recovery from this area, it may resume its move toward $45, where there was some selling pressure previously. A wider range of resistance is seen in the $47-48 zone, a previous consolidation area before the prior breakdown.

All other technical evidence is negative. In its technical summary for November, Investing.com said silver is a "strong sell" as the RSI was below the neutral 50 level and the majority of moving averages indicated selling pressure.

What Traders Should Watch Next?

The first question that needs to be asked is if silver can sustain the $40 support level during a resumption of trading. If prices fall below it, then the bearish argument would be reinforced, and if they rise above it, perhaps for the first time, it would suggest that selling pressure is easing.

US dollar, Treasury yields, and Federal Reserve communications should also be watched by traders. Any further improvement in yields and a stronger dollar will remain a headwind for non-yielding precious metals. However, if the economy releases weaker data or the policy stance is less hawkish, there will be a chance to recover.

Industrial-demand expectations are also an element to consider, as silver is used in the manufacturing sector as well as the monetary market. Even if gold stabilizes, the prospects for buying will be constrained by signs of weaker industrial activity.

The technical picture is currently tilted towards sellers. For traders to assert that the recent pullback is over, they must get some of that nearby resistance cleared before the big move to the downside resumes. Until then, the $40 level is the key price to look at for a possible stabilization versus another leg lower.

data.title: CBOT soybeans rally, supported by stronger Brazilian real, export demand
data.description:
Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures rallied to a one-month high on Friday on support from a stronger Brazilian real, higher soymeal prices and steady export demand for US soybeans.

  • Brazilian assets rallied after President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva tapped a market-friendly bank executive to be his next finance ‌chief, following weeks of investor concern over the fiscal direction of the leftist leader's upcoming fourth term.

  • Export demand for soybeans has also been steady.

  • The US Department of Agriculture reported net weekly export sales of 755,800 metric tons of soybeans. The agency also reported sales of 132,000 tons of soybeans to the Netherlands for 2026/27 delivery.

  • Investors are weighing whether exports to China will be affected, as the top soy importer was already on pace to meet its annual purchasing commitment, while a disappointing harvest in South America could shift demand toward US soybeans.

  • The soy complex received support from rising soymeal futures, which have climbed on expectations that European Union demand could rise due to the bloc's new deforestation rules set to take effect in late December.

  • CBOT January soybeans rose 22-1/4 cents to $12.66-1/4 a bushel.

  • CBOT January soymeal (SMF27) ended $4.20 higher at $362.30 per short ton, a 5-1/2-week high.

  • CBOT January soyoil ended 0.92 cent higher at 59.29 cents per pound.

data.title: ECB's next rate move will probably meet market expectations, Vujcic tells paper
data.description:
The European Central Bank's next interest-rate decision will probably be in line with the market's expectations of a rate rise, ECB Vice President Boris Vujcic said in an interview with Austrian newspaper Kurier published on Friday.

"As things currently stand, I think market expectations will probably become true, as long as nothing unexpected happens in the meantime," the newspaper quoted Vujcic as saying in a joint interview with Austrian ECB policymaker Martin Kocher when asked about the next rate-setting meeting next month.

data.title: Oil Futures Settle Lower Ahead of OPEC+ Policy Meeting — Market Talk
data.description: Oil futures end the session lower with the market awaiting the weekend meeting of OPEC and its allies to discuss output policy for 2027. The gathering in Vienna will be "one of the most complicated OPEC+ meetings in years," Jorge Leon of Rystad Energy says in a note. The war in the Middle East has made current production a poor guide for what members can sustain, and "they are being asked to set quotas for a market whose 2027 balance depends entirely on how fast the Strait of Hormuz reopens to commercial traffic, which none of them controls." WTI settles down 0.7% at $83.08 a barrel for a 0.4% weekly loss. Brent falls 1.2% to $95.44, but snaps a three-week losing streak with a 3.1% weekly gain. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

data.title: CBOT wheat edges higher in light trading
data.description:
Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures ticked higher on Friday amid light holiday trading and spillover support from rising soybean futures.

  • Traders continue to keep a close eye on the ongoing conflict in the Black Sea.

  • Ukraine has offered a Black Sea ceasefire to enable food exports and passed this on to international allies, Kyiv's foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said on Friday.

  • Russia's Foreign Ministry accused Latvia on Friday of creating artificial obstacles to hinder the transit of Russian grain to global markets, saying the restrictions posed additional risks to global food security.

  • Russian Arctic seaport of Murmansk has signed a contract to ship 600,000 metric tons of grain for export by September 2027, the port's managing company said on Friday.

  • The company disclosed neither the supplier nor the buyer.

  • Trade volume has been relatively light between Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday and ahead of the weekend. Grain markets were closed for Thanksgiving and traded for an abbreviated session on Friday.

  • CBOT March wheat settled 3-1/2 cents higher to $5.91 per bushel.

  • K.C. March hard red winter wheat (KWH27) settled 5-1/2 cents higher to $6.36 per bushel.

  • Minneapolis March spring wheat (MWEH27) settled 7 cents higher to $6.53-1/2 per bushel.

data.title: Precious Metals Rally as AI Trade Revives Risk Appetite — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni and Adam Whittaker

Precious-metal prices surged Friday as investors returned to the artificial-intelligence trade and global stocks rebounded, boosting risk appetite and easing pressure on assets that had been sold to meet liquidity needs.

Front-month gold futures rose 2.9% in New York to $3,639.60 a troy ounce for a weekly gain of 3.5%. Silver rose 7.8% to $43.167 a troy ounce, its largest single-day percentage gain since Feb. 3, and was up 5.1% on the week. Platinum rose 6% to $1,313.90 a troy ounce. The gains offer some relief, but all three metals remain significantly lower year to date.

Copper futures rose 3.4% Friday to $5.5170 a pound.

The rally also lifted mining stocks in London, with the sector leading gains on the FTSE 100. Friday's advance follows a challenging period for mining companies, whose shares have come under pressure as metal prices weakened and concerns about the AI trade weighed on investor sentiment.

Silver and gold miner Fresnillo shares rose 4.8%, while its peer Endeavour Mining gained 3.1%. Copper producer Antofagasta climbed 4.4%. Diversified miners Glencore and Anglo American, both with significant exposure to copper, advanced 4.3% and 3.8%, respectively. Valterra Platinum's London-listed shares gained 7.8%.

"Beyond the technical nature of the rebound, the recovery also highlights the role of precious metals as an ATM in times of market stress," analysts at Saxo Bank said. "With AI-related technology stocks rebounding and broader risk appetite improving, the queue at the cash machine appears to be thinning, easing the liquidity-driven selling pressure."

Still, the broader macroeconomic backdrop remains challenging. Traders are pricing in a quarter-point rate hike at the Federal Reserve's next policy meeting in December, while attention is also turning to whether the U.S. central bank will signal further monetary tightening for 2027.

Higher interest rates can weigh on nonyielding assets such as gold and silver by making interest-bearing investments relatively more attractive.

Write to Giulia Petroni at giulia.petroni@wsj.com and Adam Whittaker at adam.whittaker@wsj.com
